newsitem.title: CHINA: Chinese dismiss charges of Democratic funding.
newsitem.headline: Chinese dismiss charges of Democratic funding.

text.p: Beijing on Monday dismissed as fabrication allegations that the Chinese government may have given money to the U.S. Democratic Party for the 1996 presidential election campaign in the United States.
"China has always seriously observed the principle of non-interference in the internal affairs of other countries," a Foreign Ministry spokesman said.

"This particular report that the Chinese Embassy in Washington has been involved in the provision of contributions to the Democratic Party of the United States is a fabrication and is made with ulterior motives," the spokesman said.
"We want to express our utmost displeasure at such totally irresponsible reporting," he said.

The Washington Post reported last week that the U.S. Justice Department had found evidence that the Chinese Embassy was used for planning contributions to the Democratic National Committee before the 1996 presidential campaign.
President Bill Clinton has backed a "thorough" investigation into the allegations, saying he had no knowledge of the charges, but said "they obviously have to be thoroughly investigated."
It is illegal for a foreign government or foreigners in most cases to donate to U.S. election campaigns.
